preview: Interview experience of Rushabh Jain for an FTE role at PwC, detailing the aptitude test, technical round, partner round, and HR round.
content: Interview Experience AUGUST 2023 Prepared By: Rushabh Jain Final Year B. Tech Mechanical VJTI, Mumbai Rushabh Jain rushabhjain116@gmail.com linkedin.com/in/rushabhjain116 About PwC Eligible Branches: Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering. Eligibility Criteria: 60% Aggregate (This is not equivalent to 6 CGPA), No Backlogs. Hiring Workflow: 1. Aptitude Test, 2. Technical Round, 3. Partner Round, 4. HR Round. Role: Technology Consultant & Risk Consultant. Location: PAN India. CTC: 9 LPA. Aptitude Test: The aptitude test was conducted on 17th August 2023 on hirepro platform with online proctoring. It was a 60 minutes test with 45 questions. This is the most important stage as only 50% applicants got shortlisted. The level of test is medium to hard and not easy. Questions were mainly from Data Interpretation (pie charts, bar graphs), Verbal Ability (reading comprehension, synonyms, fill in the blanks), Quants (HCF & LCM, mixture, ratio & proportion), Logical Reasoning (seating arrangement, alphanumeric series), etc. Indiabix is a good start but the difficulty level there is too easy and you should upgrade it. Faceprep offers good alternative for practice & mock tests once you've good grip over the fundamentals. Career Ride YouTube channel can be referred to clear the concepts. Technical Round: All three Interview Rounds were scheduled online for 23rd August 2023 on the superset interview platform. The technical round lasted for 15-20 minutes and started with an obvious question "Tell me about yourself". The interviewer then took me off the cards and started asking random questions like what's special about today. I was aware of the Chandrayaan-3 landing and Praggnanandhaa playing CWC finale. He seemed happy with my answer. Based on my introduction, he asked "Why shorter content is excessively consumed then longer content on social media?". He asked some situational based questions based on my introduction like "What policies will you make to curb distraction of YouTube shorts & Instagram Reels in youth if you're the Minister of India?". He again throwed a thought provoking question "How much time it will take for India to become a manufacturing based economy?" and "Why India still imports even smallest of the smallest item? Don't we have the capacity to manufacture them?". My answers were precise, confident, diplomatic and flooded with knowledge. The interviewer basically wanted to check my knowledge, thought processing, pressure handling and communication skills in this round. The interviewer always gives you a window to take the interview in the direction you want. Make sure you use that window. Partner Round: A senior person referred as 'partner' in the organization conducts this round and it lasted for 20 minutes for me. The first question itself was a banger "Why your grades look average? We need students who're academically strong". Then he asked my current & previous semester subjects and my favourite one from them. I stated all of them and Project Management (PM) as my favourite. The interviewer dug deep into the concepts of PM and asked some real life examples where PM can be applied and how it can be applied. "Is it applicable to a software project? Can we consider a trip to Goa as a Project? Justify your answers". He later routed to my summer internship experience and what was my experience there. He gave me a situation that "What will be your reaction if your manager criticizes me in front of my colleagues?". I had some good Positions of Responsibility mentioned in my resume and he was curious to know about my experience there and how it has enhanced me as an individual. My interests & hobbies were asked by him which again I explained with much clarity & in depth. "Are you planning for Masters? If yes then why should I hire you as you'll leave the organization soon and if not then why not?", he enquired. "What do you know about PwC?" was his next question. "Why you took Mechanical at first place when CS-IT was booming and now you again want a Tech role? You seem very confused regarding some important decisions in your life". I was completely grilled by his counter questions but still managed to answered them all. The Interviewer asked me if I have any questions for him to which I responded yes and my question was "What a typical day at work looks like at PwC in the Technology Consultant Role?". He explained me what my day-to-day responsibilities would be and the Interview ended on a good note. All the questions revolved around my resume. Avoid bragging in resume as it can turn out to be negative since someone who has years of experience can catch it immediately. This was tough round for me but what made me through is again handling pressure and honestly answering all the questions. How I react to various situations was examined. Staying calm can get you through this round. HR Round: Everyone who survived till HR Round got placed as this round is just a formality. It lasted for 10 minutes. HR started with "Tell me something about yourself which is not in your resume" for which I was prepared. She enquired about my family background. She later asked some most common questions like "What are your strengths & weaknesses?", "Why PwC?", "Why should I hire you?". She confirmed that am I comfortable for travelling frequently and what if I have to be at a client place for several weeks which is in a tier-3 city. The Interviewer asked me if I have any questions for him to which I responded yes and my question was "How frequently promotions occur at PwC and what's the organization hierarchy & office culture?". The results were announced on the same day by 10:30 PM and I was extremely happy to see my name up there :) Tips & Resources: Sincerely prepare aptitude as it will be helpful for all future companies. Be confident, calm and good at effective communication. Strictly avoid bragging or over exaggerating in resume. Be thorough with each and every line in the resume and topics revolving around it. Practice some frequently asked interview questions beforehand. Attend PPT carefully as it will help in answering questions like "Why PwC?", "Why should we hire you?" and most importantly "What do you know about PwC?". Try to align with core values of the organization. Keep faith. All the best! For Aptitude: https://www.indiabix.com/, https://www.faceprep.in/, https://www.youtube.com/@CareerRideOfficial.
